title: Windows Service Created Referencing A User-Writable Path
detection_hypothesis: If persistence is installed as a service, the Service Control Manager installation event will record an image path in a directory writable by non-administrative users.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.Provider_Name: Name of the event provider that raised the record.
field_semantics.ImagePath: Executable path configured for the service, including arguments.

collection_prerequisites: The System event log is collected from endpoints and servers.
Service Control Manager events are not filtered out by the forwarder subscription.
expected_collection_gaps: Service installation performed by driver loading is not represented here.
Servers with aggressive System log filters may drop Event ID 7045.
normalization_assumptions: ImagePath contains the full service binary path including any arguments.
ingestion_differences: Quoted service paths may or may not retain surrounding quotation marks.
Some pipelines rename ImagePath to service.executable.
retention_considerations: System log volume is low; 365 days of retention is generally affordable.
expected_volume: Very low; each match warrants review.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches are short lived, appear during change windows, and use predictable service names. Tune on ServiceName combined with the maintenance window rather than on the path fragment.
tuning_guidance: Exclude specific ServiceName values used by approved installers. Do not exclude the temporary directory fragments, because they are the core of the detection.
test_strategy: Positive cases install services from the machine temporary directory and the public directory. Negative cases use a managed program directory, a non-service event, and a different provider.

attack_techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
